spec_source: GrowthIM v4 Universal Algorithm Spec — Batches 1-12

tier_definitions.1: Peer-reviewed — academic publications in indexed journals
tier_definitions.2: Institutional / industry-association — government, trade bodies, large vendor research with disclosed methodology
tier_definitions.3: Vendor research — disclosed-source vendor data (Womply, Boulevard, Bedford, etc.)
tier_definitions.4: Consultancy — McKinsey, Bain, BCG industry reports

citation_policy.rule: Every customer-facing claim in a GrowthIM report MUST reference at least one study.id in this registry.
citation_policy.tier_3_disclosure: Tier-3 studies must include a vendor disclosure in the customer report.
citation_policy.supersession: When a Batch-11 sector-specific study supersedes a Batch-9 cross-industry study for the same NAICS-2, the sector-specific study takes precedence.

studies.claim: 1-point increase in independent hotel reputation index lifts ADR by ~11%
studies.citation: Anderson, C. K. (2009). The Billboard Effect: Online Travel Agent Impact on Non-OTA Reservation Volume. Cornell Hospitality Report, 9(16).
studies.finding_summary: Cornell Center for Hospitality Research analysis of independent hotel reputation indices and revenue performance. A 1-point reputation lift on a 100-point scale corresponds to ~11% ADR increase.
studies.methodology: Cross-sectional analysis of independent-hotel data with reputation index from review-aggregation platforms.
studies.sample: Independent U.S. hotels; specific n in Cornell working-paper series.
studies.limitations: Pre-2010; OTA landscape has shifted. Reputation-index methodology is proprietary. Use as directional for chain-vs-independent framing.

studies.claim: 1-point reputation gain → ~9% RevPAR lift across full-service hotels
studies.citation: Anderson, C. K. (2012). The Impact of Social Media on Lodging Performance. Cornell Hospitality Report, 12(15).
studies.finding_summary: Follow-up to S001 across full-service properties (chain and independent). 1-point reputation gain on TripAdvisor / Travelocity rating index correlates with ~9% RevPAR lift.
studies.methodology: Cross-sectional regression with property-level controls.
studies.limitations: Effect attenuates for branded chains (~30% smaller). Methodology shifted from S001 (different reputation-index source).

studies.claim: TripAdvisor rating elasticity: 1 percentage-point lift in good ratings → ~1.4% RevPAR
studies.citation: Anderson, C. K. & Han, S. (2017). Hotel Performance Impact of Socially Engaging with Consumers. Cornell Hospitality Report, 17(5).
studies.finding_summary: Engaging with reviews (responding to good and bad) measurably moves RevPAR. 1pp lift in good-rating share → ~1.4% RevPAR.
studies.methodology: Panel-data analysis of hotel financial performance vs review-response activity.
studies.sample: Cornell consortium hotels — chain and independent.
studies.limitations: Selection effect: hotels that respond to reviews may already be operationally better.

studies.claim: Hotels responding to >40% of reviews see RevPAR lift; >65% sees diminishing returns
studies.citation: Anderson, C. K., et al. (2014). Online Reviews and Hotel Performance. Cornell Center for Hospitality Research.
studies.finding_summary: Response-rate to reviews has a non-linear effect: lift between 0-40%, plateau 40-65%, diminishing returns above. Optimal response budget targets 40-60%.
studies.methodology: Threshold regression on response-rate vs RevPAR.
studies.limitations: Response-quality varies; 40% with low-quality replies underperforms 30% with high-quality replies.

studies.claim: Restaurant industry sales projected ~$1.1T in 2025; 87% of operators say recruiting/retaining is a top challenge
studies.citation: National Restaurant Association. (2025). State of the Restaurant Industry Report.
studies.finding_summary: Industry-wide TAM proxy: $1.1T sales 2025. Labor remains operators' top challenge (87%); food costs second (74%). Customer-experience gaps and tech adoption follow.
studies.methodology: Annual NRA survey of multi-thousand U.S. restaurant operators.
studies.limitations: Industry-association data; reflect operator perceptions, not customer behavior.

studies.claim: 1-star Yelp lift → 5-9% revenue lift at INDEPENDENT restaurants; no significant effect at chains
studies.citation: Luca, M. (2016). Reviews, Reputation, and Revenue: The Case of Yelp.com. HBS Working Paper No. 12-016.
studies.finding_summary: Regression-discontinuity design exploiting Yelp's rating-rounding rule. 1-star rating increase → 5-9% revenue lift at INDEPENDENT restaurants. Chain restaurants show no significant effect — chain brand-equity dominates Yelp signal.
studies.methodology: Regression-discontinuity using Yelp's half-star rounding as the cutoff.
studies.sample: Several thousand Seattle restaurants over multi-year window.
studies.limitations: Single-market study (Seattle). Effect sizes likely vary by market, cuisine type. Chain finding is critical for GrowthIM's chain-detection logic.

studies.claim: Restaurants with 100+ Yelp reviews earn 25-30% more than those with <10
studies.citation: Womply. (2019). The State of Local Restaurants. Vendor research report.
studies.finding_summary: Cross-section of restaurant revenue vs Yelp review count. 100+ review threshold associates with 25-30% revenue premium.
studies.methodology: Cross-sectional analysis of restaurant POS data joined with Yelp metadata.
studies.limitations: Vendor research; selection bias (Womply customers self-select). Cross-sectional, not causal.

studies.claim: Industry gym/fitness studio member retention averages 66.4%
studies.citation: Health & Fitness Association (HFA). (2025). Member Retention Benchmark Report.
studies.finding_summary: Industry-wide member retention 66.4%. Boutique studios outperform big-box (~70% vs 60%). 90-day onboarding window critical: members who don't return in first 90 days have <20% one-year retention.
studies.methodology: Annual industry survey of HFA member organizations.
studies.limitations: HFA-member-only sample; non-member operators may differ.

studies.claim: Gyms with structured 30-60-90 day onboarding see ~40% retention lift over no-onboarding peers
studies.citation: Bedford. (2024). Gym Member Onboarding Outcomes. Vendor white paper.
studies.finding_summary: Structured 30/60/90-day check-ins lift one-year retention by ~40% relative to gyms without formal onboarding. Most lift is in days 30-90 — pre-90-day attrition is the decisive cohort.
studies.methodology: Cohort comparison across Bedford-platform gyms.
studies.sample: Several hundred gyms on Bedford platform.
studies.limitations: Vendor research with selection bias; effect-size attribution to onboarding alone is incomplete.

studies.claim: Local businesses with 200+ reviews earn 2x revenue of businesses with <10
studies.citation: Womply. (2022). The Reviews-Revenue Multiplier. Vendor research.
studies.finding_summary: Cross-industry: businesses with 200+ Google reviews earn ~2× revenue of those with <10 reviews. Effect strongest in service categories (auto, salon, restaurant); weakest in commodity retail.
studies.methodology: Cross-sectional analysis joining POS data and Google review counts.
studies.limitations: Vendor research. Cross-sectional. Volume correlates with age of business and many other things.

studies.claim: Reviews ≤90 days old correlate with ~30% higher revenue than businesses with reviews >180 days old
studies.citation: Womply. (2022). Review Recency and Revenue. Vendor research.
studies.finding_summary: Recency matters as much as volume. Businesses whose most-recent review is <90 days old earn ~30% more than those with >180-day-old most-recent reviews.
studies.methodology: Cross-sectional analysis with recency cutoffs.
studies.limitations: Vendor research. Selection: actively-managed businesses get more recent reviews AND have other operational advantages.

studies.claim: Bad ratings on Google hurt revenue 33%; Yelp 19%; Facebook 9%
studies.citation: Womply. (2022). Platform-Specific Review Impact. Vendor research.
studies.finding_summary: Platform matters. A bad Google rating hits revenue 33%; equivalent on Yelp 19%; Facebook 9%. Google is the dominant signal — recovery resources should prioritize Google.
studies.methodology: Cross-platform comparison.
studies.limitations: Vendor research. Magnitudes are directional; absolute values depend on industry and market.

studies.claim: E-commerce conversion rate increases 354% from 0 reviews to ≥100 reviews; review presence is THE single largest conversion lever
studies.citation: PowerReviews. (2022). The Growing Power of Reviews. Vendor research.
studies.finding_summary: Sliding scale of review-count vs conversion: 0 reviews vs 1-10 = 52% lift; 11-30 = 90% lift; 31-100 = 175%; 100+ = 354%. Lift compounds; ratings are second-order to volume.
studies.methodology: PowerReviews-platform conversion data across thousands of e-commerce SKUs.
studies.limitations: Vendor data. Causality unclear: high-conversion SKUs attract more reviews.

studies.claim: Retail businesses with 43+ Yelp reviews earn 26% more; with 200+ reviews 46% more
studies.citation: Womply. (2019). The State of Local Retail. Vendor research.
studies.finding_summary: Sector-specific retail finding: 43-review threshold = 26% revenue premium vs <10. 200+ reviews = 46% premium. The 43-review number is what distinguishes 'discoverable' retail from 'invisible' retail.
studies.methodology: Cross-sectional analysis of retail POS data joined with Yelp metadata.
studies.limitations: Vendor research; selection bias (Womply retailers). The 43-review-threshold has been replicated across multiple Womply reports.

studies.claim: 98% of consumers read reviews of local businesses; 87% read reviews before professional service
studies.citation: BrightLocal. (2024). Local Consumer Review Survey.
studies.finding_summary: 98% of consumers read online reviews of local businesses (up from 81% in 2018). 87% read reviews before choosing a local professional service. Reviews <3 months old carry significantly more weight than older reviews.
studies.methodology: Annual consumer survey.
studies.limitations: Self-reported behavior. BrightLocal is a SEO vendor; aligned-incentives caveat.

studies.claim: 0.1-star Google rating increase correlates with ~25% conversion lift for brick-and-mortar businesses
studies.citation: Uberall. (2023). Reputation Management Insights.
studies.finding_summary: 0.1-star rating change has measurable effect: ~25% conversion lift for brick-and-mortar. Sharpest effect in the 3.5-4.5 star band; minimal below 3.5 (filtered out by users) or above 4.5 (skepticism).
studies.methodology: Uberall-platform conversion data.
studies.limitations: Vendor research. Selection effect: well-rated businesses are usually well-operated. The 0.1-star granularity is the actionable insight.

studies.claim: 5pp customer-retention lift translates into 25-95% profit lift across industries
studies.citation: Reichheld, F. F., & Sasser, W. E. (1990). Zero Defections: Quality Comes to Services. Harvard Business Review.
studies.finding_summary: Foundational customer-retention finding. 5 percentage-point retention lift produces 25-95% profit lift, varying by industry. Banking, insurance, professional services see the highest end (75-95%); commodity retail the lower end (25-40%).
studies.methodology: Bain & Company industry-by-industry analysis.
studies.limitations: 1990 data. Replicated multiple times since (Bain Loyalty Effect series). Direction robust; magnitude varies by industry.

studies.claim: Companies in top quartile of CX outperform peers on revenue growth by ~2x over 5 years
studies.citation: McKinsey & Company. (2021). The State of Customer Experience.
studies.finding_summary: Top-quartile CX firms grow revenue ~2x peers over 5 years. CX leaders also see 1.5x lower acquisition costs and ~2x higher employee engagement.
studies.methodology: McKinsey panel analysis across multi-thousand companies.
studies.limitations: Consultancy research with directional findings. Magnitudes are illustrative.

studies.claim: 73% of consumers consider CX a deciding factor in purchase; 65% pay more for better CX
studies.citation: McKinsey & Company. (2023). The Customer Experience Decade in Review.
studies.finding_summary: 73% of consumers cite CX as a deciding factor in purchase (up from 56% in 2014). 65% will pay a premium for better CX. Findings consistent across consumer-good categories and services.
studies.methodology: Consumer survey panel.
studies.limitations: Self-reported; aspirational responses inflate willingness-to-pay-premium figures.

studies.claim: 92% of consumers trust friend/family recommendations above any advertising; 81% need trust to buy
studies.citation: Edelman Trust Barometer (2024) + Nielsen Global Trust in Advertising (2021).
studies.finding_summary: 92% trust friend/family recommendations (Nielsen). 81% require trust to make a purchase decision (Edelman). Trust is the dominant intermediate variable between reviews/referrals and revenue.
studies.methodology: Annual cross-country surveys.
studies.sample: Edelman: 32K+ in 28 markets. Nielsen: 30K+ in 60 countries.
studies.limitations: Self-reported; cross-country averages mask variation.

studies.claim: Construction firms with structured post-project feedback see 15% higher margins and ~$1.8M in referral revenue
studies.citation: ClearlyRated. (2025). Benchmarks, Insights, and Trends: Client Experience in the AEC Industry.
studies.finding_summary: AEC firms with structured post-project feedback see 15% higher gross margins and average ~$1.8M additional referral revenue. 78% of buyers say seamless CX influences rehire/refer decisions.
studies.methodology: Annual benchmark survey of AEC firms.
studies.limitations: Vendor research with selection bias. Use as 'firms that adopt this practice see' framing.

studies.claim: Holt Homes lifted referral sales 25%→35%+ and NPS 6.0→73.1 over 4 years
studies.citation: Bokka Group. (2025). Holt Homes Referral Growth Case Study.
studies.finding_summary: Single-firm case: 4-year structured CX program lifted referral sales share from 25% to 35%+ and NPS from 6.0 to 73.1.
studies.methodology: Single-firm longitudinal case study.
studies.limitations: Single-firm case; vendor incentive. Use as illustrative ceiling, not baseline expectation.

studies.claim: Google LSAs deliver 31% close rate vs 2x Thumbtack and 3x Angi; Angi CAC ~$2,500 vs SEO ~$300
studies.citation: Blue Grid Media. (2026). Angi vs Thumbtack vs HomeAdvisor: Contractor Lead-Gen Benchmarks.
studies.finding_summary: Channel-mix CAC spread: SEO ~$290-310; LSA $800-1,500; Angi ~$2,500. LSA close rate 31%; Thumbtack ~15%; Angi ~10%.
studies.methodology: Aggregated managed-account data plus published platform benchmarks.
studies.limitations: Vendor incentive (LSA agency). Direction robust across multiple sources.

studies.claim: 59% recognize physician-review-website importance; 35% pick on good ratings; 37% avoid on bad
studies.citation: Hong, Y. A., et al. (2019). What Do Patients Say About Doctors Online? J Med Internet Res, 21(4), e12521.
studies.finding_summary: Systematic review of physician-rating-website research. Strong evidence reviews influence patient choice across specialties.
studies.methodology: Systematic literature review.
studies.sample: Aggregated primary studies covering tens of thousands of patient surveys.
studies.limitations: Pre-pandemic data. Generalizes across specialties — dental and specialty patterns may differ.

studies.claim: Dental patient online reviews correlate strongly with CAHPS Dental Plan Survey performance measures
studies.citation: Chen, X., et al. (2020). Assessing Patient Experience and Healthcare Quality of Dental Care Using Patient Online Reviews. J Med Internet Res, 22(7), e18652.
studies.finding_summary: 204,751 U.S. dentists from HealthGrades; reviews correlate with CAHPS measures. Significant associations with online presence, education, years of practice.
studies.methodology: Mixed-methods informatics analysis: statistics + NLP + expert evaluation.
studies.limitations: Cross-sectional. Single-platform sample (HealthGrades).

studies.claim: 80%+ of dental reviews positive consistently; admin pain points (phone, scheduling) drive most complaints, not clinical care
studies.citation: Hopcraft, M. S., et al. (2025). Patient perceptions of English dental services. British Dental Journal, 239(2).
studies.finding_summary: Sentiment + topic analysis pre/during/post-pandemic. Persistent finding: admin > clinical for complaints. Phone, scheduling, expectation-management are highest-leverage targets.
studies.methodology: Sentiment analysis + topic modeling of online reviews.
studies.sample: Tens of thousands of NHS dental reviews across years.
studies.limitations: U.K./NHS context; U.S. differs in insurance/access. Direction (admin>clinical) is robust across healthcare.

studies.claim: 82% of legal clients seek reviews; 81% seek referrals; 50.6% are highly influenced by online reviews
studies.citation: Clio. (2021, 2023). Legal Trends Report and Understanding the Legal Consumer.
studies.finding_summary: Reviews + referrals dominate legal-client discovery. Multi-platform presence (Google + Avvo + 1 more) required.
studies.methodology: Annual consumer survey + practice-management platform data.
studies.limitations: Clio is a vendor. Findings consistent across multiple annual reports — directionally robust.

studies.claim: Referred customers in professional services: 16% more profit, 37% higher retention, 30% better conversion
studies.citation: Schmitt, P., Skiera, B., & Van den Bulte, C. (2011). Referral Programs and Customer Value. Journal of Marketing, 75(1), 46-59.
studies.finding_summary: Foundational referral-economics study. Referred customers have higher lifetime value across multiple metrics. Each referred customer makes 2.68 follow-on referrals.
studies.methodology: Long-term study of bank customer cohorts.
studies.limitations: Original study in retail banking. Direction generalizes; magnitudes vary across professional services.

studies.claim: 87% read reviews before choosing a local professional service; review influence is HIGHER in legal/medical/financial than in retail
studies.citation: BrightLocal. (2024). Local Consumer Review Survey — Professional Services Subsegment.
studies.finding_summary: Higher-stakes services see more review-reading; consumers consult more platforms (Google + Avvo + Yelp for legal; Google + Healthgrades + Vitals for medical).
studies.methodology: Subsegment analysis of annual BrightLocal consumer survey.
studies.limitations: Self-reported. Smaller subsegment; refresh annually.

studies.study_type: industry benchmark — local-services lead-gen channel CAC
studies.claim: 8x CAC spread across local-services channels: SEO $300, LSA $800-1500, Angi $2500
studies.citation: Aggregated industry benchmarks (Adapt Digital, Blue Grid Media, ProWeb365 — 2026).
studies.finding_summary: Channel mix is the dominant marketing decision for local-services SMBs. Aggregator (Angi/Thumbtack) CAC routinely exceeds revenue per booked job for typical service calls.
studies.methodology: Aggregated managed-account data across multiple agencies.
studies.limitations: Vendor-aggregated. Magnitudes vary by trade and market; direction robust.

studies.study_type: industry — synthesis of Nielsen + Edelman + trade-press
studies.claim: 92% trust friend/family above advertising; word-of-mouth drives 60-70% of new clients in local services
studies.citation: Synthesis: Nielsen Global Trust 2021, Edelman Trust Barometer 2024, plus QuickBooks/Angi/HomeAdvisor industry-share data.
studies.finding_summary: Local services rely on referrals more than other sectors. Review-management is referral-amplification; reviews are not standalone marketing.
studies.methodology: Multi-source synthesis.
studies.sample: Nielsen + Edelman aggregate; trade-press industry-share estimates.
studies.limitations: 60-70% figure is trade-press estimate, not peer-reviewed. The 92% trust figure is robustly peer-validated.

studies.claim: Auto repair shops lose 50-60% of customers year-over-year; NADA recommends 72%+ service-department gross retention
studies.citation: Auto Apps / R.O. Writer (2024) + NADA Service Department Whitepaper.
studies.finding_summary: Industry baseline retention 40-50%; NADA target 72%+. Returning + best customers (3+ visits, $1800+/yr) should be 70-80% of monthly revenue.
studies.methodology: Auto Apps longitudinal cohort analysis + NADA benchmark.
studies.limitations: Auto Apps is vendor-affiliated. NADA represents franchised dealers. 50-60% non-return is consistent across multiple sources.

studies.claim: Salon online-bookers return ~78% vs walk-ins ~39%; 46% of bookings happen outside business hours
studies.citation: Boulevard. (2023). Salon Industry Trends Report.
studies.finding_summary: 24/7 online booking is the highest-ROI single intervention for an independent salon. Caveat: selection bias means causal incremental lift is closer to 1.3-1.5x, not 2x.
studies.methodology: Boulevard-platform observational analysis.
studies.limitations: Vendor research. Selection: online-bookers self-select for commitment.

studies.claim: Escape rooms / experiential entertainment: 70%+ of new bookings driven by online reviews; 3-5x conversion uplift with 50+ reviews
studies.citation: Room Escape Artist Industry Reports (2023-2024) + IBISWorld.
studies.finding_summary: Experiential entertainment 70%+ review-driven. Reviews <3 months disproportionately weighted (consistent with Womply S011).
studies.methodology: Trade-press surveys + market research aggregation.
studies.limitations: Trade-press, not peer-reviewed. Generalizes to other non-gym recreation with varying magnitudes.

studies.claim: Golf and bowling: ~50% review-driven, ~30% channel-app, ~20% direct-channel discovery
studies.citation: National Golf Foundation (NGF) + Bowling Proprietors Association of America (BPAA) Industry Reports.
studies.finding_summary: Golf courses (713910) and bowling centers (713950) have unique discovery mix: 50% reviews, 30% category apps (GolfNow, BowlerX), 20% direct.
studies.methodology: Trade-association annual operator surveys.
studies.limitations: Operator self-report. May overstate apps and understate referrals (apps have direct attribution; referrals don't).
